exercise.question: Define like and unlike parallel forces.
What are rectangular components of a vector and their values?
What is the line of action of a force?
Define moment of a force. Prove that τ = rF sinθ, where θ is angle between r and F.
With the help of a diagram, show that the resultant force is zero but the resultant torque is not zero.

Identify the state of equilibrium in each case in the figure given below. [Figure: Three illustrations labelled (a), (b), and (c): (a) a cone resting on its circular base; (b) a ball on top of a dome; (c) a cylinder lying horizontally on its side.]
Give an example of the body which is moving yet in equilibrium.
Define centre of mass and centre of gravity of a body.
What are two basic principles of stability in physics which are applied in designing balancing toys and racing cars?
How can you prove that the centripetal force always acts perpendicular to velocity?
A car travels at the same speed around two curves with different radii. For which radius the car experiences more centripetal force? Prove your answer.
A ripe mango does not normally fall from the tree. But when the branch of the tree is shaken, the mango falls down easily. Can you tell the reason?

Discuss the concepts of stability and centre of gravity in relation to objects toppling over. Provide an example where an object’s centre of gravity affects its stability, and explain how altering its base of support can influence stability.
Why an accelerated body cannot be considered in equilibrium?
Two boxes of the same weight but different heights are lying on the floor of a truck. If the truck makes a sudden stop, which box is more likely to tumble over? Why?
Explain the principle of moments with an example.
Describe how could you determine the centre of gravity of an irregular shaped lamina experimentally.
State and explain two conditions of equilibrium.
How the stability of an object can be improved? Give a few examples to support your answer.
A force of 200 N is acting on a cart at an angle of 30° with the horizontal direction. Find the x and y-components of the force.

A force of 300 N is applied perpendicularly at the knob of a door to open it as shown in the given figure. If the knob is 1.2 m away from the hinge, what is the torque applied? Is it positive or negative torque? [Figure: A door with hinges along its left edge, a knob on the right edge, a dashed line from the hinge to the knob labelled 1.2 m, and a force arrow labelled F.]

Two weights are hanging from a metre rule at the positions as shown in the given figure. If the metre rule is balanced at its centre of gravity (C. G), find the unknown weight w. [Figure: A metre rule balanced on a support labelled C.G, with a weight w hanging 40 cm to the left and a 4 N weight hanging 30 cm to the right.]

A see-saw is balanced with two children sitting near either end. Child A weighs 30 kg and sits 2 metres away from the pivot, while child B weighs 40 kg and sits 1.5 metres from the pivot. Calculate the total moment on each side and determine if the sea-saw is in equilibrium.

A crowbar is used to lift a box as shown in the given figure. If the downward force of 250 N is applied at the end of the bar, how much weight does the other end bear? The crowbar itself has negligible weight. [Figure: A box rests at the left end of a crowbar angled upward to the right. The bar is supported near the box; the distances shown are 5 cm from the box to the support and 30 cm from the support to the downward force F at the right end.]

A 30 cm long spanner is used to open the nut of a car. If the torque required for it is 150 N m, how much force F should be applied on the spanner as shown in the figure given below. [Figure: A horizontal spanner with its head at the left and a nut at the right; a vertical force F is applied at the right end, with a horizontal dashed line extending to the right.]

A 5 N ball hanging from a rope is pulled to the right by a horizontal force F. The rope makes an angle of 60° with the ceiling, as shown in the given figure. Determine the magnitude of force F and tension T in the string. [Figure: A ball hangs from a slanting rope attached to a horizontal ceiling. The angle between the rope and ceiling is 60°. The rope is labelled T, and a horizontal arrow pointing right toward the ball is labelled F.]

A signboard is suspended by means of two steel wires as shown in the given figure. If the weight of the board is 200 N, what is the tension in the strings? [Figure: A signboard is suspended by two vertical wires labelled T_1 and T_2. The distances from the centre to the wires are marked 2 m on each side. The board is labelled “Signboard”, with a downward arrow labelled 200 N.]

One girl of 30 kg mass sits 1.6 m from the axis of a see-saw. Another girl of mass 40 kg wants to sit on the other side, so that the see-saw may remain in equilibrium. How far away from the axis, the other girl may sit?

Find the tension in each string as shown in the given figure, if the block weighs 150 N. [Figure: A joint is connected to a horizontal string at the right and a slanting string to a horizontal support above. The angle between the slanting string and the horizontal support is 60°. A block hangs below the joint and is labelled 150 N.]
